Summary: Portable, 3-D printed slanting adaptation for a standard hardboard clip board.
Who: People with Filum Disease have difficulty controlling eye movements and processing shapes and forms, which makes reading difficult. Looking down with the neck bent can also cause pain and vital sign issues.
Why: Slant boards are used to help with reading because of how it stabilizes the letters' shapes to be easier to process. They also bring papers to a higher level to prevent bending the neck. Most are not portable which makes it hard to transport where needed.
How: It is smaller, lighter, and more transportable which allows it to be brought to all places where reading support is needed while protecting the board. It also will not take up as much space and removes glare issues present in other slant boards.
What: This is a 3D printed attachment that snaps onto any clipboard, turning it into a slant board at the recommended 25 degree angle. It also comes apart to fit in a quart size bag which makes it light, compact, and easy to transport in a backpack. Tools needed FDM Printer

Summary: The 3D-Printed Toddler Mobility Trainer (3DTMT) is an affordable, open-source device that empowers young children with disabilities to explore their environment independently. Designed for indoor use, it fills the gap in early-age mobility options, especially for toddlers who lack the strength or coordination to crawl or walk and have limited access to age-appropriate wheelchairs. By enabling seated, arm-driven movement, the 3DTMT provides a practical, easily manufactured solution that promotes early mobility, engagement, and development.
Who: The 3DTMT is an affordable, open-source solution designed to support independent mobility for young children in indoor environments.
Why: Many toddlers and young children with disabilities lack the physical strength or coordination needed to crawl or walk independently-- even though they may be ready to explore and engage with their environment. Wheelchair options for this age group are rarely available, affordable, or covered by most insurance providers.
How: This product helps kids learn to move in a seated position using their arms and/or hands, providing increased mobility for those with limited lower limb strength.
What: An affordable and easily manufactured mobility trainer suitable for younger ages in indoor environments. Inspired— and informed by— the original TOM Toddler Mobility Trainer, this newly-designed model brings together the ease of 3D printing and the expertise of our partners, collaborators and Need-Knowers. A design collaboration between LINK PBC, Tikkun Olam Makers, and MakeGood. Solution Name: Custom Arm Prosthesis - Lightweight Parametric Prosthetic Arm
Summary: This solution is an inexpensive, quick-to-manufacture, 3D printed custom parametric prosthesis for below-the-elbow amputees. This prosthesis is the base unit that is connected to the arm and can be paired with different end units for a variety of functions for daily tasks or recreational activities (See below).
Who: Below-the-elbow amputees who hope to achieve greater independence in every day actions, such as working in the kitchen, playing the guitar, playing basketball and more. We worked with 8 different Need Knowers throughout the development process.
Why: For amputees, a prosthesis is often a necessity. However, there are no effective low-cost custom prostheses available on the market. Therefore a person that needs a prosthesis, usually can afford/ will receive from health care, only one. Getting a customized prosthesis today requires a lot of time and money, and most need to be replaced every few years.
How: Utilizing 3D printing and parametric design enables this prosthesis to be both affordable and easily customizable for a comfortable fit for all users. It is designed to connect to a system of end units to remain multifunctional despite not being robotic. Our manufacturing process is cheap, simple & fast, so any makerspace center (e.g., a TOM community) can produce it.
What: This solution is an inexpensive, quick-to-manufacture, 3D printed custom parametric prosthesis for below-the-elbow amputees. Summary:
An affordable device that supports children with disabilities in crawling and quadruped movement-- providing secure positioning and head support, and freeing caregivers' hands to engage more actively with the child.

Who: Children roughly 18 months and older who still need quadruped positioning and crawling practice-- to develop shoulder and hip stability, depth perception and protective responses.

How: The Coggon Crawler provides secure positioning+head support so a child with limited strength/head control can safely practice crawling, while a caregiver's hands are free to engage, encourage, and interact face-to-face instead of supporting their weight.

Solution Name: Tube Opener - Unscrew Caps with Ease!
Summary: This entirely 3D-printed device was designed as a tool to open containers with screwable caps that range from about 10–25 mm in diameter. Tube Opener was designed by Makers Making Change. To learn more, visit their website at https://makersmakingchange.com/
Who: The Tube Opener is designed for people who have trouble unscrewing small caps - whether it is due to arthritis or any limitation regarding finger/hand movement.
Why: Unscrewing caps takes a great deal of force and precise finger movements that can be challenging for many people. This device was designed to allow people to open and close their items independently and with ease.
How: Place the Tube Opener down on stable surface. Position the tube to be opened so that the tube cap is located within the working grip area of the opener. Press down on the opener to grip the cap, and twist the tube to unscrew the cap. The guard along the back and the thumb rest helps stop fingers curling into the working grip area. Tools Needed: 3D Printer Bill of Materials: Please see BOM and printing models in the downloadable product file. Estimated Time to Make: 1.5 hours of machine time
What: The Tube Opener help open tubes or small lids for anyone that has difficulty gripping and twisting the caps. The tool is designed for tube caps that range from about 10–25 mm in diameter, typically 12–50 ml capacity. This device is entirely 3D printable. This device can be used to open: Toothpaste or ointment Hot sauce, condiment jars, vanilla extract, apple cider vinegar Paint supplies Travel size products Nail polish and remover And more!

Summary: The Clearly Mask is a DIY transparent face mask design to make Coronavirus safety measures more accommodating for lip readers. While the mask was specifically designed to benefit people with hearing impairment, we recommend it for everyone looking to benefit from more visible communication and human connection. To see the tutorial please see the resources section below.
Why: People with hearing impairments often rely on lip reading to understand others interacting with them. Mask wearing during the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as in medical environment, hamper their ability to understand and interact with people in their environment.
How: The product is comprised of fabric, straps, and clear pvc that are sewn together to create a clear mask with the mouth visible. You can download the assembly guide and patterns from our website www.tomglobal.org, and sew a mask (or more!). TOM Clear Mask - how to sew tutorial ! from TOM Global on Vimeo. Our aim at TOM is to enable as many people as possible to have a product that fits their needs. Clear masks are in high demand, but there aren’t many open source products tackling this problem. Our objectives are: 1. To offer an open-source design that is safe to use, referencing medical requirements and standards. This affected our choice of fabric and our suggestion to seal the sewing holes. (Note: This product has not been approved for medical use or tested by health authorities, but it follows the guidelines published by the Israeli Ministry of Health). 2. To develop a mask that offers the best user experience, both in terms of comfort (ease of breathing, ease of putting on and taking off), and functionality (a large clear area to maximize the visibility of facial expressions which allows easy and clear communication). Technology: Sewing machine Laser cutter (optional - you can cut the patterns by hand) Materials: We sourced materials based on The Israeli Ministry of Health’s recommendations for fabric masks. These include: White Cotton Sateen fabric with a thread count of 200 or higher. The transparent window made of 0.25mm PVC. Anti-Fog Spray and / or Dish Soap Care instructions: Easy to clean, machine washable at 60 degrees Celsius. Open Source Development: We are calling on you to join our collaborative R&D process and help us find the safest solutions to these issues: 1. Finding the best head strap configuration for people with hearing aids. 2. Ensuring as little exposure as possible around the mouth and nose area due to needle holes in the seams surrounding the clear window (our current DIY solution: covering the seam with medical tape). Is there a better non-industrial option? We are currently running a usability test in our communities and we’re inviting you to join! Have you tried to sew a Clearly Mask? Please fill out this design feedback form and let us know how to make it better. Have you used the Clearly Mask? Please fill out this user feedback form  and let us know about your user experience.
What: The Clear Mask is a DIY transparent face mask design to make Coronavirus safety measures more accommodating for lip readers. While the mask was specifically designed to benefit people with hearing impairment, we recommend it for everyone looking to benefit from more visible communication and human connection.

To follow updates on PJ Prosthesis, other assistive tech solutions by TOM communities, and our global network of makers, follow us on social media here. Product Development History PJ Prosthesis is a universal platform that enables the continuous development of modules and attachments, both custom-made and generic, to accommodate a wide array of functionalities and features for different users of different sizes. Development of the PJ Prosthesis platform began in 2018 when TOM’s Tel Aviv community created a lightweight yet durable 3D printed prosthetic arm for IDF veteran Noam Guez. After losing his left arm in basic training, Guez wanted a comfortable device to regain his independence in daily tasks and beloved hobbies like cooking (especially Shakshuka) and painting. TOM: Singapore adapted the platform in 2019 to accommodate the needs of Tan Wee Boon, a Quadruple Amputee who lost his limbs to a flesh-eating bacteria, resulting in the PJ Prosthesis Double Amputee Module. This new module employs generic functions for double upper-limb amputees, such as easily attaching and removing the device independently using a pull string, as well as tailor-made sizing and functionality to allow the user, Boon to shower and use the toilet independently. Additional developments in Singapore include refining the prosthesis base to boost the appeal and creating a grip for holding spoons and bottles. See the PJ Prosthesis Double Amputee Module here. Most recently, TOM: Shenkar outfitted the prosthesis with two new specialized attachments to the modular limb to allow Yael and Itamar (27) in Israel to play the violin and drums respectively. These developments took place at the annual Merkaha or Jam Week at Shenkar College of Engineering and Design in Israel, where Shenkar’s TOM community held a 72-hour makeathon. Additional PJ attachments developed at the TOM: Shenkar Makeathon includes a smartphone holder for Itamar, and a chef’s knife attachment for Ester. “TOM communities hope to develop multiple product lines of modular device attachments for PJ to enable amputees to regain freedom of function and pleasure in the arts, crafting, and more,” says Daniel Levy, Head of TOM R&D. Levy heads the development of PJ, along with two other industrial designers from Tel Aviv. PJ Prosthesis has been featured in Channel News Asia, the Jerusalem Post, and Baltimore Jewish Life. Changing the World with a Modular Prosthesis by TOM from TOM Global on Vimeo.

Solution Name: What mechanism can we develop that allows a safer reception of packages?
Summary: During the past 2 weeks, we have been virtually working non-stop on developing a solution to ensure safe package deliveries. After various days of research and brainstorming, our team has developed two prototypes and one protocol to ensure this happens. We developed two prototypes thinking about all of the populations socioeconomic status, our first prototype, the PICKUP BOX is a simple but effective was to disinfect your products at home, it consists of a carton box being wrapped with a plastic bag where you can place most deliveries and form a safe distance disinfect and receive packages. This prototype allows homeowners to get there package with minimum to 0 risks of infection. This is accompanied by simple protocols that allow families to learn how to deal with the different elements that enter their homes through any kind of package that is being delivered, the information obtained for this protocols was taken form government official websites and health announcements by the OMS. The second prototype, the Package Cleaner was built to focus on buildings, company's, and restaurants. This prototype consists of a spray system composed of 6mm diameter hoses, 5 racks or T's and 4 specific spray nozzles for this type of hose, these accessories are distributed so that the spray nozzles are located in the four upper corners of the box,  It also has a 12V DC motor pump which is activated by means of a switch and performs the function of pushing the disinfectant from its reservoir or tank to the spray nozzles with sufficient pressure to generate the effect of spraying throughout the interior of the box. The structure of the box is made of PVC pipes and accessories and is covered with a heat and moisture resistant plastic. The protocols we attached to both prototypes as additional information was obtained from at least 5 credible sources.

Solution Name: What solution can we propose so the children can do mobility exercises and stimulation at home?
Summary: Amidst the COVID-19 pandemic, my team and I were presented with a brand new challenge! Quarantining has brought a new task to all parents, and our problem states just that. So look forward to the best option for your children, which is extremely affordable, as well as good en efficient on developing motor skills.

Solution Name: How can we keep disinfected when educational institutions open again?
Summary: The group came up with various ideas to solve the issue. First of all, we came up with a kit. The purpose of the kit is to maintain yourself clean. It includes three different prototypes which all have the same purpose: keeping us clean. The first device is a bottle holder. By having an antibacterial bottle at the reach of your hands you would wash your hands with a greater frequency. Also, having a personal bottle would decrease the risk of contagion. The second device is a modified umbrella. The modified umbrella would be mainly used in places like cafeterias. The umbrella has polyethylene flexible sheets around it to protect the user and the whole community. The modified umbrella has on the bottom part support that allows the umbrella to stand still on a desk or cafeteria. The third and last device is a hook that helps the user open doors and uses ATMs without directly touching the handles and ATMs. We also created a face shield that is designed especially for kids. The mask is made especially for kids and even young adults. It is made with a design and size that is perfect for kids. The purpose of the mask is to make sure that kids are excited to wear a mask, therefore, protecting their health and the health of the whole community. To continue the group came up with a device that would protect the students while they are in class. The device is made mainly for classrooms that are not very big and have many desks which makes it harder to spread the desks to maintain the 2 m distance. This device is made so that there is protection surrounding the desk which decreases the chances of contagion. The device is made up mostly of PVC tubes and acetate sheets. The structural support of the device is the PVC tubes, which are connected to the legs of the chair on the right side. What truly protects the user are the acetate sheets that cover the back and right side of the desk. Finally, the group created a circuit with some sensors. Solution Name: How can we protect those working in access points?
Summary: The protective booth for personnel access points includes various parts and accessories, all made with the intention of creating a safer environment for the staff at the access points and the people around them. Unquestionably, the protective cabin is the main piece of our design since it is where the personnel at the entrance is completely safe while developing its tasks. It is a cabin that covers the front and sides of the person, made of PVC pipes and acrylic screens that protect the person in it from any type of germ, contact, or saliva. In addition, our design has a Gun Type Digital Infrared Thermometer which will serve to take people’s temperature when passing through the cabin. The person in the cabin will have the thermometer, and when a person arrives at the entrance he will take out the thermometer through a hole in the acrylic screen and without any physical contact will determine if the person is in good health conditions to enter the place. Furthermore, right next to the cabin will be located a pedal-operated gel dispenser made of PVC tubes which will be used on a mandatory basis for people who are close to the cabin. The dispenser will have a specialized Antibacterial gel with expert approval called Klaxin fco x 60 tan, (this gel has no side effects on people’s bodies). In addition, our design includes a disinfectant shoe mat made from cheap and recyclable materials, such as a 20-liter bottle, artificial grass, and foam. This accessory will be located just in front of the cabin and will be used by everyone entering this space. Finally, our design is open to receive your own variations that best suit your own needs.

Solution Name: How can we protect the healthcare personnel?
Summary: After having investigated and analyzed the possible sources of contagion for health personnel, the EscafMED project team has leaned towards developing a diving suit used by medical personnel in intensive care units to prevent COVID-19 contagion, since this is the place where they take the patient in the most critical stage of the disease. It is a closed and very small area (15 m2), in which the health personnel remains caring for the patient more than the time necessary to be infected, obtaining a high probability of acquiring intra-hospital infections, also generating high levels of stress at the personal, social and family level; because it can be frowned upon as a source of contagion since when accessing this space, direct contact is made with the virus in its most aggressive and fatal stage. After having a broad vision of the spaces and problems faced by health personnel within hospitals and clinics when caring for patients with positive results for COVID19, the team that today presents EscafMED led by Julián Andrés Zuñiga and Andrés Torres launched into the challenge of creating this prototype, a technological innovation that seeks to prevent the spread of COVID19 in medical personnel who enter the ICU, without leaving aside a design that generates greater comfort for those who use it. So far, facial protection designs that have a good virus macromolecule filter generate facial discomfort.

Summary: Head Tilt Sensor and Indicator
Who: Some patients with neurological impairments aren't able to recognize when their head is significantly tilted. This can potentially lead to muscle strain and other issues. Therefore, this project aims to provide solutions to patients to help them.
